office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding, ferries and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Two Democrats: three-term Rep. Tarra Simmons, who faces a $52,000 state ethics penalty she is appealing, against first-time candidate Daria Ilgen, a former tech strategist running on fiscal discipline and accountability. Simmons won the primary about 57% to 39%; they differ on new taxes, spending, policing and housing.

candidates.summary: Attorney and former nurse in the House since 2021, now Deputy Speaker Pro Tempore, known for criminal-justice, reentry and health-care legislation; the Legislative Ethics Board fined her in 2026 and she is appealing.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and 2025 capital gains, estate and B&O tax increases [S18][S20][S22]
Authored prior-authorization, charity-care and mental health parity laws [S6]
Voted against Initiative 2081 (2024) and co-sponsored its 2025 rewrite, HB 1296 [S26][S28]
Sponsored the ICE Out Act (HB 2641), which died in committee [S15]
Ethics board found three violations; penalty with costs is about $52,000, under appeal [S12]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346 and 2025 B&O and capital gains/estate tax increases; platform calls for asking more from those who can afford it.

spending.basis: Platform calls for more state investment in housing, schools and child care, but she backed cutting Blake legal-aid funding as wasteful during a shortfall.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217 rent and fee increase limits, said rent prices must be stabilized, backs social housing and more public housing investment.

safety.basis: Centers treatment, reentry, root causes and police accountability; voted against I-2113 restoring police pursuits.

climate.basis: Supported the Climate Commitment Act and voted for the 2024 clean-energy transition bill; platform targets major polluters.

experience.basis: Three-term incumbent and Deputy Speaker Pro Tempore with a list of authored laws, running on 'proven leadership'.

immigration.basis: Lead sponsor of HB 2641 to bar police from hiring post-2025 ICE officers; supported immigrant worker protections.

healthcare.basis: Health agenda works within the existing system: insurer prior-authorization rules, charity care, parity and drug costs; no single-payer statement.

social.basis: Pledges to defend gender-affirming care and LGBTQIA+ protections, championed abortion-care protections, endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against I-2081 and co-sponsored and voted for HB 1296, which narrowed its parental rights and added student privacy rights.

candidates.summary: Former strategist for Amazon, Zillow and Expedia, Democratic Party officer and Kitsap nonprofit board member, running on fiscal discipline, affordability and accountability; has not held public office.
highlights: Taxpayer Accountability Standard: five questions any new tax must answer before he votes for it [S8]
Platform calls for audits, performance measures and ending ineffective programs [S6]
Endorsed by AWB, NFIB, Kitsap Builders, Realtors and two police organizations [S7]
Proposes limits on surveillance pricing and a TRUST Act on surplus campaign funds [S9][S10]

taxes.basis: Sets a five-question test before any new tax and says he will not oppose every tax, while calling for tax equity and targeted relief.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for audits, performance measures, cutting waste and reviewing existing spending first, while protecting essential services.

housing.basis: Housing plank centers cutting red tape, faster permitting and density; no rent-regulation position.

safety.basis: Pledges law-enforcement staffing and tools, endorsed by WACOPS and Poulsbo police; also backs mental health and addiction services.

climate.basis: Supports transit-oriented growth to cut carbon emissions and environmental protection; no Climate Commitment Act position.

experience.basis: Has not held public office and runs on 'new leadership' and fresh thinking against a three-term incumbent.

reform.basis: Proposes the TRUST Act tightening rules on surplus campaign funds and conflicts of interest.

immigration.basis: Pledges to stand up for immigrant families so they can live without fear.

healthcare.basis: Health plan holds insurers accountable and expands providers within the current system.

social.basis: Pledges to protect LGBTQ+ neighbors and reject intolerance; no statements on sports eligibility or abortion.

tech.basis: Would require disclosure of data-driven pricing and ban use of sensitive personal data to price essential goods.
